Lessons.Title: Domain and Range (Part 2)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: infer domain and range directly from features of graphs, including open/closed endpoints, horizontal segments, holes, and discrete inputs, and interpret restrictions in context. Original Edulytiks source-aligned lesson based on Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 11, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/11/preparation.html and student tasks https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/11/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source compares continuous, step and oscillating graphs rather than relying only on function formulas.

Original fictional delivery charge step graph: C(t)=4 dollars for 0≤t<2 hours, C(t)=7 for 2≤t<4, and C(t)=10 for 4≤t≤6, where t is elapsed service time. Input domain [0,6], output range exactly {4,7,10}; it is incorrect to claim every cost between4 and10 occurs. At t=2, the left segment ends open at cost4 and the next begins closed at cost7.

Original continuous triangular ride-height graph joins (0,0),(3,9),(7,0) with straight segments. Domain [0,7] seconds and range [0,9] metres, because all intermediate heights are attained under the interpolation assumption. Compare a continuous interval of outputs with a step function's isolated set of outputs.

Student task: draw both graphs with accurate open/closed points; decide whether a graph includes certain inputs and outputs; compare two graphs with identical x-domain but different ranges; and explain why a jump in graph excludes intermediate output values. Teacher-scored rubric 0–2 for endpoints, domain, range and coherent context explanation with suitable accessible alternatives.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph domain
KeyConcepts.Definition: All x-coordinates represented by points of a function graph.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Watch open endpoints and missing x-values.
KeyConcepts.Example: For delivery C, domain [0,6] includes 0 and6.

KeyConcepts.Title: Graph range
KeyConcepts.Rule: Do not fill between discrete or stepped outputs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Open versus closed endpoints
KeyConcepts.Definition: A filled circle includes a point; an open circle excludes it.
KeyConcepts.Rule: At a shared boundary choose the rule that contains equality.
KeyConcepts.Example: At t=2 the cost is7, not4.

WorkedExamples.Title: Read domain and range from step segments
WorkedExamples.Question: Find domain and range of C(t)=4 on [0,2),7 on [2,4),10 on [4,6].
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact first-party function definition and independently verify each substitution, graph feature and domain.
Steps: The three time intervals cover every t from0 through6.
Every segment is horizontal and takes one of only three values.
No cost of6 dollars is attained.
WorkedExamples.Check: Check closed endpoints match the stated intervals.

WorkedExamples.Title: Handle boundary accurately
WorkedExamples.Question: What is C(2) and C(4)?
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact first-party function definition and independently verify each substitution, graph feature and domain.
Steps: At t=2 the first piece t<2 is excluded.
The middle piece 2≤t<4 applies, giving C(2)=7.
At t=4 the middle piece excludes equality.
The last piece 4≤t≤6 applies, giving C(4)=10.
WorkedExamples.Check: At each input exactly one value is assigned.

WorkedExamples.Title: Contrast a continuous triangular graph
WorkedExamples.Question: The ride joins (0,0),(3,9),(7,0) with straight segments. Find range.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use the exact first-party function definition and independently verify each substitution, graph feature and domain.
Steps: The ride is defined from t0 through t7 inclusive.
It rises continuously from0 to9 then falls continuously to0.
All heights between0 and9 occur on a segment.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Replacing a step range with an entire numerical interval
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Values such as6 are never outputs.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assigning two costs to a shared breakpoint
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Overlapping closed pieces would break function uniqueness.

SummaryPoints: A graph's x-values form its domain and its y-values form its range.
Step-function range can be discrete despite continuous input.
Teacher reviews accurate graphs and reasoning.
